beginner: Inflation cooled to 2.43% in February, right where the Federal Reserve wants it, so prices should stop rising so fast at the grocery store. But now a spanner in the works. Oil prices have risen due to the war, so prices at the gas pump are up.
The job market is holding steady with unemployment at 4.4%, meaning most people who want to work can find jobs without too much trouble.
The economy is expected to grow faster this year than most experts predicted, which usually means more wage growth and business expansion ahead.
moderate: Core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred measure, is tracking toward the 2.2% target by year-end, suggesting rate cuts may continue even as headline CPI at 2.43% remains slightly above that goal. The Fed has room to ease further without reigniting price pressures.

Unemployment at 4.4% remains below the Fed's estimated natural rate, but labor market cooling has been gradual enough that inflation is falling without a severe jobs crisis, unlike the 2022-2023 cycle.
GDP growth is forecast to reach 2.8% this year, well above the consensus 2.2% estimate, implying stronger consumer spending and business investment than the market currently prices in.
expert: Core PCE inflation at 2.2% by December 2026 represents a 120 basis point decline from peak, achieved without unemployment spiking above 4.5%, suggesting the soft-landing scenario is materializing. The policy rate at 3.64% in February signals the Fed is roughly 25-40 basis points into its easing cycle, with downside risk to rates if growth outpaces the 2.8% forecast.

February CPI print of 2.43% sits 23 basis points above the year-end PCE target, but disinflation momentum remains intact. If goods deflation persists and wage growth continues moderating, the Fed could reach 2.5% policy rate by Q4 2026.

The 2026 GDP forecast of 2.8% versus 2.2% consensus reflects stronger household balance sheets and pent-up capital expenditure than current market pricing captures, though the 6.9% fiscal deficit poses medium-term current account risks that may constrain long-duration asset valuations.
